page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources consist of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

This instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a 307 GB local SSD. No GPU accelerators are present, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core (1648.0) and stress-ng single-core CPU tests scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak. The Geekbench multi-core score (3539.0) and stress-ng multi-core performance (3869.36) fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical core limitation of a 2-core, 4-thread setup. Memory bandwidth tests also register in the bottom 25%, with uncached read and write speeds at 30.58 GB/sec and 25.35 GB/sec respectively.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the E8-4ds_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. It is suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and memory-heavy text processing. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or multi-threaded decompression, where benchmarks indicate poor to weak performance.
